Ph.D. Ted Kaczynski writes:

"..In the United States, a couple of decades ago when leftists were a
minority in our universities, leftist professors were vigorous proponents of
academic freedom, but today, in those universities where leftists have
become dominant, they have shown themselves ready to take away from everyone
else's academic freedom. (This is 'political correctness.)'  [216]

"Today, in those of our universities where 'political correctness' has
become dominant, there are probably many leftish types who privately
disapprove of the suppression of academic freedom, but they go along with it
anyway." [225]


Now, if we get rid of our preconceived notions and biases with regard to
Ted, we will see that much of his views sound very familiar with how other
adacemics and scholars feel.   While it has been implied that his Manifesto
gives evidence of his "paranoia", the truth is that no one would even
suspect him to be mentally unstable if he had not been caught; in other
words, it's only after the fact that people say, "look at his Manifesto and
you'll see that he is warped."

It frightens people to think that such a rational, coherent being as
Kaczynski could commit such gruesome crimes.   Such labels as "insane" and
"psychopath" then become arbitrarily used to paint Ted as a monster.  The
simplistic code of morality they have been taught growing up in their
church, mosque or synogogue provides a framework that allows them to evade
ambiguities in life.

That's not to say that Kaczynski is a "cool" guy; but just because he
committed murder does not negate his 160-170 IQ, or mean that he is
necessarily a schizophrenic -- or even discredits his Manifesto!  This is
propaganda used by oversocialized media moguls to vilify him, to fulfill
what they believe is their role in molding public opinion to their brand of
secular humanism.

;o)

"We have a system of quality control in scholarship. It is called criticism.
This has broken down when it comes to feminist research. Scholars are not
correcting the faulty research for fear of appearing illiberal or 'sexist.'
This has done terrible harm already."

-- Christine Hoff Sommers

"..It's also interesting to note that the women's studies and black studies
departments, which were originally set up to fight the intolerance of
traditional academic departments, are now among the most intolerant places
on campus. In a history course, if you write a paper suggesting the French
Revolution was terrible, you don't worry that it will affect your classroom
standing. But if you stand up in a women's studies class and say you think
abortion on demand is wrong, this generates enormous discomfort, and you
have to watch out for your grade.

"..Years ago, young Marxists didn't say, 'I'm a Marxist and I'm right about
the world.' They said, 'Don't censor me; let me say my piece.' But then when
they became chairmen of their departments, free speech became an irritant
that was put aside."

-- Dinesh D'Souza

"Today, many campus radicals from the 1960's are the tenured radicals of the
1990's. They have become the chairs of departments, the deans, and the
chancellors of the universities: senior political administrators in Congress
and Houses of Parliament, and even the presidents and prime ministers of
countries. The 1960's mentality of peace, love, and above all, equality, now
constitutes the intellectual dogma of the Western academic world. There are
laws to prohibit platforms for those denounced as 'fascists' and others
deemed to be not politically correct."

-- J. Philippe Rushton (Anthropology, University of Western Ontario)
